sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Leveraged Buyout Acquisition Syndicate and Special Purpose Co

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) – freedom of establishment and capital movements
France–United States Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion (active, as amended)
France–China Agreement for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (active, as amended by 2010 Protocol)
France–Germany Double Taxation Agreement (active, as amended)
France–United Kingdom Double Taxation Agreement (active, as amended)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier) Art. L561-2 et seq., L561-10 and R561-1 et seq.; French Commercial Code (Code de commerce) Art. R123-163 to R123-178 (RBE/UBO register); Decree No. 2019-1335 of 11 December 2019; Ordinance No. 2020-115 of 12 February 2020; Regulation (EU) 2015/847; Directive (EU) 2015/849 as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized/certified copy of passport or national identity card for each natural-person UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent authority in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; if the issuing state has not acceded to the 1961 Hague Convention, consular legalization by the French Embassy/Consulate is required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized proof of residential address for each UBO (utility bill or bank statement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public utility provider or financial institution, certified by a notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation/extract from the foreign registry for any corporate UBO or PE fund sponsor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of the country of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incumbency/register of directors and shareholders of the ultimate PE fund or holding entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company secretary or corporate services provider of the ultimate entity

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank KYC/reference letter covering the PE fund and syndicated lending group
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original bank letter sent directly to the French incorporation counsel; no apostille is normally required, but notarization of signatory capacity may be requested by the French bank

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP, OFAC, UN and EU screening of all UBOs, directors and signatories; screening must cover the OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council consolidated list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list and the French Direction générale du Trésor asset-freeze list; enhanced due diligence is mandatory for non-resident corporate UBOs, for any PE fund with state-linked investors, and for any person holding foreign public-office positions or family/close-associate connections; TRACFIN/SAR filing obligations under L561-15 apply.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises – formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (operated by INPI); official registry data published through the Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés (RNCS) and accessible via Infogreffe.fr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The SAS corporate name must be submitted in the Latin alphabet and in French script for legal documents; a foreign-language name is permitted only if transliterated/romanized and if all supporting statutory documents are filed in French; the name must be distinctive and not likely to mislead the public, and it must include or complement the legal form 'SAS' or 'Société par actions simplifiée' as required at registration.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: French law does not provide a separate statutory name-reservation shelf; the 30-day validity is the internal pre-clearance confirmation issued by French incorporation counsel. If the Guichet unique/Greffe rejects the proposed name, the applicant may (i) obtain a written statement of grounds, (ii) file an amended incorporation dossier with a modified distinctive name, or (iii) within the applicable judicial time limit, bring a summary challenge before the President of the competent Tribunal de commerce. If rejection rests on a prohibited or regulated token, the appropriate ministerial or professional-authority authorization must be obtained before resubmission; otherwise the name is permanently unusable for the proposed SAS.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditional: a French SAS may be domiciled with an approved domiciliation company for a maximum initial period of two years, subject to a written domiciliation contract and tax-administration notification; a pure virtual mailbox without any local operational or decision-making capacity is not permissible for a PE buyout SPV and will not satisfy French commercial/substance requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Elevated: 70% likelihood within the first 36 months for a passive, zero-employee leveraged-buyout SPV with foreign UBOs; unannounced physical inspections may be carried out by DGFiP, the Greffe du tribunal de commerce and anti-money-laundering authorities (ACPR/TRACFIN) to verify host-country economic substance and the reality of the registered office.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting and bilingual legal review of the French SAS articles of association (statuts)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (typical fixed drafting fee or hourly rate of EUR 250–EUR 450)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name availability search and preliminary clearance certificate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark/registry tariff for corporate-name due diligence

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille/consular legalization of UBO identity, address, incorporation and incumbency documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority in origin state plus French Consulate, as applicable
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official government fee per document plus consular service charge

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code, Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 and R.227-1 et seq. governing the Société par Actions Simplifiée; Articles L.123-1 et seq. governing registration; Articles L.561-46 et seq. governing beneficial ownership declarations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent Greffe of the Tribunal de Commerce or designated commercial court registry for the registered office, with the Registre National des Entreprises administered by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic application for registration and commencement of activity submitted through the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by INPI, accompanied by the executed SAS articles of association and beneficial ownership declaration.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital applies to an SAS. The articles must state the capital amount and share terms. At least 50% of cash contributions must be paid upon subscription, and the balance must be paid within five years of registration. Cash contributions are generally deposited into a blocked account or with a notary before incorporation, against a deposit certificate; funds are released after issuance of the registration extract. Legal-publication fees, beneficial ownership fees, notarial fees, and bank charges are excluded from the stated filing fee. The USD amount is an indicative conversion of the applicable French registration charge and must be verified at filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The undersigned, acting as the Company's initial management body, resolve that: (1) the Company accepts the subscription for all issued shares in accordance with the articles and the deposit certificate, with the subscribed capital recorded in the share register; (2) the registered office is established at [full French address]; (3) [name] is appointed President for an unlimited term, subject to the articles; (4) [name] is appointed Directeur Général, if applicable; and (5) the President is authorised to complete registration, beneficial ownership filings, bank formalities, tax registrations, and all ancillary acts required to commence the Company's corporate purpose. The resolution is approved and signed on [date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm Structure, Corporate Purpose, and Governance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company founders, counsel, and the future registered-office provider; no governmental pre-clearance is normally required.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the SAS form, shareholder identity, ownership percentages, capital amount, share classes, acquisition-SPV purpose, President, optional Directeur Général, duration, financial year, transfer restrictions, and registered office. Ensure the corporate purpose covers acquisition, holding, financing, and disposal of participations and related financing activities without representing that the company performs regulated banking, investment-services, or fund-management activities.
required_dossiers: Corporate shareholder certificates of incorporation and authority documents
Registered-office agreement, lease, or domiciliation contract
Power of attorney, if filing is made by counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct inconsistent identity, purpose, address, or governance information before filing. Obtain apostilled or legalized foreign corporate documents and certified French translations where required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Subscription bank, notary, or other authorised depositary; Guichet unique submission is not yet required at this step.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the articles of association and subscription forms. Open a temporary capital account in the name of the company being formed. Transfer the cash subscription, obtain the certificate of deposit, and retain evidence of payment. Record any in-kind contribution through the required contribution documentation and, unless a statutory exemption applies, an apports auditor report.
required_dossiers: In-kind contribution agreement and auditor report, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to bank or notary compliance queries with source-of-funds evidence, shareholder ownership information, tax residence documents, and certified translations. Re-execute defective documents and obtain a replacement deposit certificate if necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: An authorised Journal d'annonces légales publisher in the department of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a formation notice containing the mandatory SAS particulars, including name, form, capital, registered office, duration, corporate purpose summary, President identity, and registration location. Obtain the publication certificate and verify that the published particulars exactly match the executed articles.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request a corrective notice promptly where a material error appears. Preserve both the original and corrective publication certificates and upload them with the registration file if requested.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Registration and Beneficial Ownership Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises, with review and registration by the competent commercial court registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create the electronic filing, select creation and commencement of activity, upload the signed articles, publication certificate, registered-office evidence, capital deposit certificate, officer declarations, identification documents, and beneficial ownership declaration. Pay the applicable charges, electronically sign the filing, and monitor the dashboard for queries. The filing must accurately identify the ultimate natural persons exercising ownership or control.
required_dossiers: Foreign-language documents with certified French translations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Answer a deficiency notice through the INPI portal within the stated deadline, upload corrected or missing documents, and pay any additional charge. If rejected, correct the identified defect and resubmit; challenge a formal registry refusal before the competent court where legally justified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Post-Registration Governance and Tax Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI, competent commercial court registry, Service des impôts des entreprises, and the company's bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the Kbis or registration extract and RNE identification. Convert the temporary bank account into the operating account and release deposited capital. Complete accounting books, share register, beneficial ownership records, tax account setup, VAT position where relevant, and corporate bank mandate. Adopt the first management resolution and preserve all corporate records.
required_dossiers: Final articles and first management resolution
Share register and shareholder account records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Escalate unresolved registry or tax-account issues through the relevant portal or registry contact. Correct corporate records by formal resolution and preserve an audit trail; amend the articles or filings where a statutory change has occurred.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable to a passive private-equity acquisition SPV with no manufacturing, storage, treatment, or physical industrial operations. If the company later operates an industrial site, the relevant authority is the Préfecture through the Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement (DREAL).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial or manufacturing operating permit is required for the stated PE syndicate SPV activity. Regulated financial activities, investment services, fund management, or public solicitation would require separate analysis and potentially authorisation from the Autorité des marchés financiers or the Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for Ecological Transition; applicable project review is administered through the competent Préfecture and the regional environmental authority, Mission régionale d'autorité environnementale (MRAe).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt or not applicable for a holding and acquisition SPV with no physical project, industrial installation, construction works, emissions, or waste-generating operations. Any later qualifying project must be screened under the French Environmental Code and may require case-by-case review or a full environmental assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No operational thresholds apply while the SPV has no physical activity. If operations commence, applicable ICPE requirements, water-discharge limits, hazardous-waste rules, air-emission and VOC limits, waste traceability, and prefectural permit conditions must be assessed before commencement.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No site-specific fire, structural-load, or occupational clearance is required for a domiciled office-only SPV beyond the obligations of the premises operator and landlord. Any occupied office or industrial premises must comply with applicable French workplace, accessibility, fire-safety, electrical, and building requirements. Industrial premises may require DREAL or Préfecture review, fire-service consultation, and occupational-risk documentation before use.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via impots.gouv.fr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must register the French SAS with the DGFiP to obtain SIREN/SIRET and VAT identification number (FR followed by SIREN). SOP requires submission of incorporation or acquisition documents, completion of tax registration forms, and activation of electronic tax account on the French tax portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections available; hybrid mismatch rules apply under French domestic law with limited specific regime elections

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time e-invoicing via France's PEPPOL network and B2B platform; invoices require digital stamp (cachet électronique) and transmission for fiscal clearance

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT rate for goods exported outside the EU or qualifying offshore services; eligibility requires proof of actual export and non-domestic use
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU), Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent claims attract 40% penalty, interest, and potential criminal prosecution; retrospective clawback of VAT credits applies

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, acting under Articles L.141-1 to L.165-2 of the French Code monétaire et financier, and in coordination with the Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution (ACPR) for banking supervision and the Eurosystem/European Central Bank for monetary policy matters. There is no separate French foreign-exchange administration; residual controls are embedded in prudential, statistics, sanctions, and foreign-direct-investment rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France maintains full convertibility for current-account transactions under IMF Article VIII; EUR payments are unrestricted. Capital-account operations are free within the European Economic Area and generally liberalized with non-EEA counterparties, subject only to EU/UN financial sanctions, anti-money-laundering verification, and prior authorization for foreign direct investment in sensitive sectors under Articles L.151-3 et seq. and R.151-3 of the Code monétaire et financier. Profit remittance by an SAS to foreign shareholders is freely executable without FX license, but is subject to French corporate-law solvency restrictions on distributions, standard AML/KYC evidence, and either domestic withholding tax relief under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or a double-tax treaty, or the applicable statutory withholding tax where no relief applies.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no statutory surrender or mandatory conversion of export proceeds. Exporters may receive and retain export receipts in any currency in authorized foreign-currency accounts held with a French credit institution or an EU/EEA passporting bank. There is no deadline for repatriation and no conversion ratio. The collecting credit institution must report cross-border flows to the Banque de France for balance-of-payments statistics; the exporter must retain invoices, customs declarations, and shipping evidence. For a private-equity buyout SPV without export activity, these rules are not applicable.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Syndicated Loan Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium as a supplementary payment/operating channel, but Low as the sole treasury rail for a leveraged buyout SPV. ACPR-licensed domestic electronic-money institutions and payment institutions, such as Qonto, Shine, or Lydia, can onboard a French SAS and provide EUR IBANs, card controls, and payment-initiation services; they cannot operate a regulatory securities escrow, settle syndicated loan funding, or provide credit. Offshore digital EMIs may legally provide e-money/payment services in France only under an EEA passport under the Payment Services Directive and E-Money Directive; an entity outside the EEA without French registration is not viable for French corporate account opening. Transactional constraints: escrow agents, notaries, and financing banks generally reject EMI accounts for closing wires, equity contributions, and buyout disbursements; therefore the SPV must maintain a Tier-1 bank relationship for all high-value capital flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose an absolute statutory requirement that every director appear physically at a bank branch if secure electronic identification is available and the client risk rating is low. In practice, French Tier-1 commercial banks require a physical or dedicated video-identification interview with at least one authorized director, the ultimate beneficial owner, or the sponsoring investment manager for a non-resident-owned private-equity SPV. Remote opening may be accepted only where the bank already maintains a verified corporate relationship, where the SPV is in a FATFA-listed jurisdiction, and where notarized certifications of identity, address, and board authority are supplied. For this buyout SPV, the recommended mandate is a physical meeting in Paris or a bank visit to the sponsor’s main office, followed by direct video interviews for all non-attending signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity of beneficial ownership chain involving offshore holding companies or managed professional entities.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete BO registry extract for each entity in the ownership chain; ultimate natural-person UBO identification documents; notarized/certified trust deed or LLP/limited partnership constitutional deed if used; corporate organizational chart with shareholding percentages; tax-residency certificates; legal opinion from French counsel confirming the economic rationale of the chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of leverage and subscription funds inconsistent with SPV purpose or insufficient source-of-wealth documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed share-subscription agreements, capital-call notices, and LPA commitment schedules; sponsor audited financial statements or investor fund statements; bank statements showing the provenance of funds; promissory note or term-sheet for the acquisition facility; independent lender legal opinion confirming bona fide lending and non-fronting.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media, sanctions exposure, or nexus with restricted Russian/Belarusian/Crimean or other sanctioned persons.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent commercial sanctions-screening report covering the SPV, shareholders, UBOs, directors, and counterparties; negative-news resolution memorandum prepared by the sponsor; written clearance opinion from French external counsel; board resolution confirming the beneficial owners are not designated persons; declaration of no nexus to restricted industries.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP status of a shareholder, director, or beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written PEP-status declaration; source-of-wealth disclosure with supporting asset and tax records; audited financial statements; notarized identity and address proof; employer/business reference; explanation of the transaction history and relationship to the buyout transaction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Apparent mismatch between stated ISIC 6499 buyout-SPV scope and requested payment rails or transaction counterparties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan and acquisition pipeline; executed or draft SPA and equity/investment agreement; projected cash-flow waterfall; transaction counterparty KYC pack; legal opinion that the SPV does not perform regulated banking, financing, or crowd-lending activity; board resolution limiting activity to buyout holding.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for an inbound equity subscription into the French SAS requires an SWIFT MT103 for non-EUR funding or a SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR funding from the investor’s account. France does not operate a statutory Chinese-style purpose code, but the remittance information field should clearly state 'CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION - SAS' together with the reference to the subscription agreement, capital-call notice, and share-allocation certificate. For correspondent-bank screening, the payer should use the ISO 20022 purpose code most consistent with the payment, as agreed in the account mandate; the key compliance element is the evidentiary bundle, not a single code. Verification at the receiving French bank will include the BO declaration, proof of identity of the transferor, source of funds, board authorization, constitutional documents, and confirmation that the capital injection is recorded in the SPV’s audited ledger. For amounts that constitute French cross-border financial operations requiring balance-of-payments statistics, the receiving bank files the report with the Banque de France; the SPV must keep the original capital-contribution deed and bank confirmation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For buyout consideration, debt-repayment, and acquisition-related trade settlements, the principal clearing rails are: SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier or registered shareholder payments; SWIFT MT202/MT202 COV for high-value nostro-covered euro or foreign-currency clearing; SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR disbursements inside EEA below high-value thresholds; commercial letters of credit under UCP600 for documented trade flows; and demand guarantees under URDG758 when escrow or warranty deposits are required. All outbound wires must reference the relevant SPA, facility agreement, or invoice, and must conform to the two-person signature mandate registered with the Tier-1 bank. The SPV should confirm that the final beneficiary, intermediary bank, and underlying transaction survive sanctions screening before release.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable OTC FX forwards in EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, and EUR/CNY with ACPR-licensed or EEA passported bank counterparties under the French FBF master agreement.
FX swaps for structural restructuring of acquisition cash flows and bridge-to-equity timing gaps.
Plain-vanilla FX options, including European calls and puts, limited to economically hedged exposure under the buyout pipeline.
Cross-currency swaps for swap of acquisition-facility interest streams into EUR or sponsor reporting currency, documented under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with appropriate collateral annex.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies with restricted convertibility, such as offshore CNH, only to the extent the SPV has a verifiable underlying payment obligation and the bank accepts non-deliverable settlement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts, allocation of profit or loss, and related shareholder decisions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders; no routine filing authority unless the decisions are filed as part of another formal change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Director liability risk, possible court injunction, and a civil fine of up to EUR 9,000 for failure to convene the required approval process; no automatic statutory strike-off deadline.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts and management report deposit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: INPI One-Stop Shop, transmitting the filing to the competent Commercial Court Registry and RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval of the accounts, or within two months after approval when filed electronically; approval must generally occur within six months after year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court injunction to file, potential civil fine, and possible director liability; repeated non-compliance may lead to registry enforcement measures or administrative radiation after formal notice, without a fixed automatic strike-off period.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return Form 2065 and statutory schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year company, by the second business day after 1 May of the following year; generally within three months after year-end for a non-calendar year, subject to the applicable electronic filing timetable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest generally at 0.20% per month and a 10% surcharge, increasing to 40% or 80% in specified circumstances; tax collection and enforcement proceedings may follow.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT return and annual VAT settlement, if subject to the normal annual VAT regime
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the statutory deadline shown in the company's electronic tax account, generally during the following year; monthly or quarterly VAT filings may also be required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest generally at 0.20% per month and a 10% surcharge, with higher surcharges for persistent or deliberate non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: INPI One-Stop Shop and competent RCS registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At incorporation and within 30 days after any change in beneficial-owner information; France does not generally require a no-change annual UBO confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court injunction, potential criminal penalties for inaccurate or omitted information, and possible registry or banking compliance restrictions; no automatic annual strike-off rule.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Appointment, renewal, or replacement of statutory auditor, where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: INPI One-Stop Shop and competent RCS registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Before the existing auditor's term expires or when statutory appointment thresholds are met; appointment filings follow the applicable corporate-formality deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Potential director liability, court appointment on application by an interested party, and criminal exposure for failure to appoint a legally required auditor; no routine annual filing if the appointment remains unchanged.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An SAS generally must appoint a statutory auditor when it exceeds at least two of the following thresholds at the financial year-end: EUR 5 million total balance sheet, EUR 10 million net turnover, and 50 average employees. Additional appointment rules apply to certain parent, subsidiary, or group situations, and a court may appoint an auditor on shareholder application.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French Generally Accepted Accounting Principles under the French Accounting Standards Authority (ANC) regulations; IFRS is generally not mandatory for separate statutory accounts of an SAS but may be used for consolidated accounts where legally permitted or required.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No standalone annual no-change confirmation is generally required. The SAS must maintain accurate beneficial-owner information and file an amendment through the INPI One-Stop Shop within 30 days after any change in ownership, control, or identifying information. Share transfers must be recorded in the register of movements of securities and in the relevant individual shareholder accounts.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of share movements and individual shareholder accounts
Register of shareholders or equivalent ownership records
Register of decisions of the president and other corporate bodies where maintained
Corporate minute book and supporting attendance and voting records
Register of directors or officers, where maintained for corporate governance and evidence purposes

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 550-2,200 per year for a standard registered-office service; France does not generally require a separate resident registered agent.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 4,000-20,000 per year for a small or medium SAS, depending on transaction volume, consolidation, leverage structure, group reporting, and audit complexity.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D tax credits, innovation status deductions, and specific tax regimes for certain sectors; no broad tax holidays

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Déclaration de résultat (Formulaire 1200-A) via impots.gouv.fr electronic filing system
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 3 months after fiscal year-end (extendable in some cases)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents report only French-source income; use simplified forms if applicable
Withholding tax already applied or reclaimable

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties of 0.75% per month of unpaid tax up to 10% maximum, plus interest on late payments
